Āṇḍavan Maṭha
------------------------------------------
Monasteries known as maṭhas as also their pontiffs, the maṭhādhipatis, have played an important role in preserving Hindu religion and culture. तपस् (austerity) and विद्या (learning) have been the bedrock of their spiritual activities.
One of the maṭhas of recent origin and perhaps less known than its counterparts is the आण्डवन् मठ of श्रीरङ्गम् (Tamil Nadu). The मठ belonging to the श्रीवैष्णव tradition and following the Viśiṣṭādvaita school of Vedānta, originated with Śrīmad Gopālācārya Mahādeśikan, also called Tirukkuḍandai Deśikar, during the middle of the eighteenth century, in कुम्भकोणम् (of Tamil Nadu). He was a man who practised severe austerities and was known for his great scholastic learning. His three disciples, continued the tradition of this great savant without break. श्रीनिवास Mahādeśikan (also known as Periyāṇdavan), the second of them, was as much a योगि of great powers as he was a monk of austerity and learning. The present pontiff, Śrī Vedānta Rāmānuja Mahādeśikan (Tirukkuḍandai Āṇdavan) the eighth in the order of succession, who was ordained in 1963 has been working hard to spread the message of his predecessors.
